summary: Design 2 (Quarry option B). Reranking of caller-supplied candidates becomes a Data Plane capability: POST /v1/rerank, served as a separate service-only sub-router inside retrieval-engine-rs and reusing the existing paid Cohere-rerank-v4.0-pro-on-Azure client. It never touches the Model Plane or any subscription route. Quarry becomes a caller: its LLM-prompt reranker, the Model Plane rerank dependency and QUARRY_EDGE__SEMANTIC_RERANK_MODEL are deleted. For ZDR orgs, sovereign requests, an unapproved processor or provider failure, the Data Plane returns the input order plus an explicit status marker, never silently. Highlights become verbatim extractive passages scored by the same cross-encoder in the same provider call. Live evidence (docker logs, auth-service registry with credentials redacted, psql aggregates, metrics) shows the two 403s have different causes, and that fixing the principal alone would expose at least four more defects behind the vector call: invalid zdr_mode "off", omitted sovereign_required, a response with no page URL, and an unscoped corpus. The design therefore also fixes Quarry's vector leg, adds principal-aware auth to the retrieval engine (default-deny route allowlist), adds metering with producer and units, adds a judged-set quality gate with score calibration for model-gateway relevance.rs, and ships contract tests that use the real registry, golden Auth Core claims and a realistic membership double instead of permissive stubs. All principal/scope changes are grouped in one Control Plane step (T01+T02). Nothing was edited, built, restarted or called (no model or paid call); only read-only live checks were made.

LEGEND: [F] verified fact (see current_state), [I] inference, [D] design decision, [O] owner decision (see owner_decisions). Nothing in this task was edited or called; live reads only.

0. WHAT THE LIVE STACK CHANGED IN THE PROBLEM
[F] The two 403s are different defects (audience for rerank; membership for retrieve). [F] Behind the retrieve 403 sit at least four more (D3 zdr_mode enum, D5 sovereign default, D6 no URL, D7 unscoped corpus) plus D4 (ZDR egress). [D] The design fixes the whole path, because a green unit test with a permissive stub is exactly how the six A6 defects survived. [F] ZDR trap: service-token zdr is a static principal posture, so Quarry must take ZDR from the request body for service callers (model-gateway, execution-core) and from the token claim only for interactive user callers.

1. THE CAPABILITY: WHERE IT LIVES AND ITS API
[D] Placement: a second sub-router on retrieval-engine-rs's existing HTTP listener (:8004), module rerank_api, sharing the existing RerankClient, JWT verifier and metrics, but NOT sharing auth_middleware (that is user-membership shaped). Not a new service. Reasons: (a) ownership matrix rows 69-71 already give rerank to retrieval-engine-rs, so a new service would duplicate provider secrets and Azure quota; (b) the engine already holds Cohere-on-Azure config, retry logic and signed cost-event plumbing; (c) auth boundary is solved by a separate service-only layer plus default-deny route allowlist; (d) blast radius is bounded by a dedicated in-flight semaphore, per-org rate class, a provider permit pool that reserves capacity for tenant-knowledge retrieval, and a kill switch (WEB_RERANK_ENABLED); (e) the contract is transport-stable so it can be extracted to its own service later without touching callers. Wire: HTTP/JSON now (Quarry's existing client style); gRPC RerankService deferred until the first Model Plane caller exists [O6]. The core is transport-agnostic (rerank_api::score) so adding gRPC later is small.

Endpoint: POST /v1/rerank (service principals only).
Request: {"request_id":"<8..64 chars, unique per org, also the metering idempotency key>", "query":"<1..1024 chars>", "documents":[{"id":"<opaque 1..128 chars, caller chooses, no URL required>","text":"<1..4000 chars>"}], "top_n":<1..documents, default all>, "profile":"web-v1", "purpose":"web_search", "highlights":{"mode":"passage|none","max_per_document":1..3}, "zdr_mode":"disabled|reject|ephemeral (optional; merged monotonically with the signed token zdr)", "sovereign_required":<bool, optional, merged>, "deadline_ms":<100..8000, default 2000>}
Limits [D]: documents<=100 (more is 400, never silent sharding of caller documents), text<=4000 chars (longer is truncated at a char boundary and listed in truncated_ids), query<=1024, body<=1 MiB (route-level limit under the global 10 MiB), unique ids, UTF-8 only. profile is an allowlist resolved server-side to a model and thresholds (web-v1 = RERANKER_MODEL); a raw model id from the caller is never accepted (the dead reranker_model field is not copied).
Response: {"request_id", "status":"ok|skipped|degraded", "reason":null|"zdr"|"sovereign"|"disabled"|"processor_not_approved"|"circuit_open"|"provider_rate_limited"|"provider_error"|"timeout"|"input_too_small", "degraded":<status!=ok>, "reranker":{"provider":"cohere","route":"azure-foundry","model":"Cohere-rerank-v4.0-pro","profile":"web-v1@1","score_kind":"cross_encoder.v1"}, "results":[{"id","index","rank","score"|null,"scored":bool,"highlights":[{"text","start_char","end_char","score"}]}], "truncated_ids":[...], "usage":{"documents_scored","passages_scored","provider_calls","search_units_estimate"}, "zdr_actions_applied":["rerank_skipped_zdr"|...], "latency_ms"}.
When status != ok, results are the INPUT order with scored:false and no scores: this is the explicit marker the owner required (never silent). Provider failure, 429 after budget, timeout, ZDR, sovereign, unapproved processor, disabled and circuit-open are all HTTP 200 with a marker so callers never retry blindly; only 400 (invalid), 401, 403, 413, and 429 from OUR per-org limiter (with Retry-After) are error statuses.
Deadline and retries [D]: the whole handler runs under tokio::time::timeout(deadline_ms); RerankClient::rerank_texts passes the remaining budget into send_with_retry, which only sleeps for a backoff or Retry-After that still fits the budget, otherwise returns degraded timeout/provider_rate_limited immediately. One provider call per request (all candidates plus passage windows, <=100 docs), no sharding, so every score in a response comes from one comparable pass.
Idempotency [D]: (org_id, request_id) is cached for 120 s in an in-process moka cache (key = blake3(org|profile|query|doc texts); value = scores and offsets only, never text) so a retry returns the identical response without a second provider call; metering idempotency key is rerank:{org}:{request_id} (deterministic, replaces the random uuid for this path).
Provider [D]: the SAME configuration as the existing reranker (RERANK_ENDPOINT, COHERE_API_KEY, RERANKER_MODEL, bearer or api-key header), called directly on Azure. Never the Model Plane, never inference-core, never a subscription route. Startup guard: web rerank refuses to enable unless RERANK_ENDPOINT is set and its host is on an Azure allowlist (*.azure.com, *.ai.azure.com), closing the public-Cohere default; a unit test pins that rerank_api imports no Model Plane client or subscription provider module.
Capacity [D]: WEB_RERANK_MAX_INFLIGHT=8; per-org class limiter WEB_RERANK_PER_ORG_RPS=5 burst 10 (Dragonfly, same fail-open convention); a shared provider permit pool and token bucket (RERANK_PROVIDER_MAX_INFLIGHT, RERANK_PROVIDER_RPS tuned to the real Foundry quota) that reserves 2 permits for tenant-knowledge retrieval; circuit breaker after 5 consecutive provider failures in 30 s (open 30 s) returning degraded circuit_open. [O1] decides shared deployment versus a dedicated Azure deployment for web traffic; recommended: shared now with the limiter, dedicated before general availability.

2. AUTHENTICATION AND TENANCY
Callers [D]: exactly one principal, quarry-edge (service:quarry-edge), audience data-plane (the engine's JWT_REQUIRED_AUDIENCE; no new audience), new scope data:rerank. quarry-control and quarry-orchestrator have no principal and are not callers [F]. Tokens are minted per org by Auth Core from the verified org of the caller's quarry token (token_for_org), scope list narrowed to [data:rerank] only; the engine independently requires: valid RS256 JWT (aud, iss, exp, nbf, boolean zdr), principal_type=service, service_id==sub, sub starts with service:, no user_id claim, non-empty scopes (mirrors documents-api-go verify.go:144-149), scope data:rerank, sub in WEB_RERANK_ALLOWED_SERVICES (default service:quarry-edge, a second belt), org_id non-empty and pinned from the signed claim (a body org is not accepted at all). No membership lookup for service principals (they are not members); tenant binding is the signed claim minted by Auth Core against the registry. Interactive user tokens can never reach it (member scopes never include data:rerank; the handler also requires principal_type=service) so it cannot become a free Cohere proxy for end users.
Principal-aware auth for the existing routes (fixes D1) [D]: new authz::principal (decision logic, in lib so integration tests can reach it; api is not in lib.rs) plus authz::service_routes, a compiled DEFAULT-DENY table of (method, path, required scope, allowed service ids): POST /v1/retrieve, /v1/retrieve/hybrid, /v1/knowledge/search require data:read for service:quarry-edge; POST /v1/rerank requires data:rerank. Every other route (admin cleanup, context pins, semantic cache, space-binding, graph/wiki/trace) rejects service principals with 403 service_principal_route_not_allowed, so skipping membership widens nothing that was not explicitly listed. User behaviour is byte-identical (membership still enforced). gRPC stays user-delegation-only (model-gateway forwards the user's bearer); an explicit test pins that.

3. ZDR, SOVEREIGNTY AND PROCESSOR BEHAVIOUR
Decision order in rerank_api::policy (pure function, table-tested): enabled? -> processor approved? -> effective zdr (signed token zdr OR body zdr_mode restrictive) -> sovereign (signed claim or body or deployment) -> circuit -> input size -> call provider. [F] What Cohere on Azure commits to is NOT established anywhere in the repo, and the code treats it as retaining egress. [D] Therefore: any restrictive ZDR posture (ephemeral or reject) returns status skipped, reason zdr, zdr_actions_applied rerank_skipped_zdr, original order, zero provider calls, zero cost event. Sovereign required returns skipped sovereign (Azure cannot satisfy it, same doctrine as orchestrator.rs:881-892). WEB_RERANK_PROCESSOR_APPROVED (default false) must be true or the capability returns skipped processor_not_approved: the operator affirms the Art. 28 processor basis for sending the QUERY to Azure/Cohere (candidates are public text; [O2] legal confirmation needed). This resolves the GDPR_SUMMARY tension: the Data Plane owns reranking and calls the provider directly by design, with the processor gate in place of Model Plane gating; GDPR_SUMMARY.md:106-108 gets a clarifying note.
ZDR made workable [D]: (a) now: skip plus marker, never silent, and Quarry surfaces rerank.status=skipped reason=zdr in its response so model-gateway can state 'results not reranked (zero-retention organisation)'; (b) dark path: RERANK_ZDR_ATTESTATION_* (resource id, approval reference, effective date, reviewer, review-by, digest) validated at startup exactly like the Azure OpenAI ZdrAttestation; only a valid, unexpired attestation lets ZDR orgs use the Azure route; no attestation exists today so it stays off; (c) option: self-hosted text cross-encoder sidecar (like colqwen-reranker/media-embedder) as profile web-v1-sovereign for ZDR/sovereign orgs, no egress [O2]. Reranking never uses a subscription or BYO route, so the user-chosen-connection ZDR prompt flow does not apply to it: the platform route is always the paid Azure Cohere deployment.
Quarry side [D]: Quarry computes effective_zdr = body.zdr OR (principal is a user AND verified claim zdr). Service callers (model-gateway, execution-core) are governed by body.zdr only (their token zdr is static). Quarry also passes sovereign_required = zero_saas_search (a posture that already promises queries never leave the cluster). rollout_and_migration: Order is fixed by two hard dependencies: the Go cost consumer decodes strictly (so it must understand new optional fields before any producer emits them) and Quarry must not run its new client before the Data Plane route and the Auth Core scope exist. Steps: (1) Wave 1 principal change set (T01+T02): edit the policy JSON by hunk (other sessions have uncommitted edits in it), run the launcher so PLANE_SERVICE_PRINCIPALS_JSON is re-assembled (it adopts existing credentials, no new secret), recreate auth-service; the new scope is inert until used. (2) Data Plane: apply the additive cost_events migration with the Data Plane migrator, rebuild and recreate data-orchestrator-go and data-quality-go, then rebuild retrieval-engine (T03,T04,T05,T06,T07,T08) with WEB_RERANK_ENABLED=0 (default) and WEB_RERANK_PROCESSOR_APPROVED=false, so /v1/retrieve for service principals and SourceRef.url are live while /v1/rerank answers skipped/disabled. Run scripts/auth-regression-matrix.sh. (3) Obtain [O2] processor confirmation, then set WEB_RERANK_PROCESSOR_APPROVED=true and WEB_RERANK_ENABLED=1 (the compose default flips to 1 in the final PR after proof). (4) Quarry: build via the launcher, deploy quarry-edge with QUARRY_EDGE__RERANK_SHADOW=1 for the smoke run (rerank called, order unchanged), then shadow off; the compose default QUARRY_EDGE__SEMANTIC_RERANK stays 1. (5) Model Plane relevance/calibration (T12) after T14. (6) Flip the ledger entry to implemented, update the matrix. DATA MIGRATION: only cost_events gains four nullable columns (existing rows keep null producer, read as retrieval-engine); no backfill, no document or index change. Config removals (QUARRY_EDGE__SEMANTIC_RERANK_MODEL, semantic_rerank_model) are harmless if the env var lingers. The gRPC proto is untouched in this design (HTTP-only SourceRef.url), avoiding a coordinated Model Plane protobuf regeneration; the drift is documented. ROLLBACK, no rebuild needed at any layer: QUARRY_EDGE__SEMANTIC_RERANK=0 restores plain merge order; WEB_RERANK_ENABLED=0 makes the Data Plane answer skipped disabled with input order; removing data:rerank from the registry makes Quarry degrade with a loud 403 marker while search keeps working; the strict service-route allowlist in the retrieval engine can be reverted independently of rerank (user behaviour is unchanged by it). Production readiness remains blocked platform-wide by the Auth Core rule that refuses allowAnyOrg principals outside development (see risks).
risks: Azure Foundry S0 per-second quota is shared by tenant-knowledge retrieval and web rerank; the engine already loses the cross-encoder on roughly 19% of queries per eval run to 429s, so web traffic can starve retrieval or lose its own rerank. Mitigation: shared provider permit pool reserving capacity for retrieval, per-org class limiter, deadline-aware retries, circuit breaker; real fix is a dedicated deployment [O1]. The actual Foundry quota is not in the repo.

Added search latency: DP rerank_ms averaged about 380-565 ms for 50 documents; budget default 2000 ms deadline with a 900 ms p95 acceptance gate; wide windows (30 candidates plus passages) raise it, which T14 sweeps measure.

Score calibration is unknown: no Cohere score calibration exists in the repo and the DP threshold 0.35 was never calibrated; until T12 lands, model-gateway's 0.6 blend and 0.30 keep threshold could over-filter sources. Interim: ship Quarry's score_kind and keep legacy semantics behind it, and do not enable on-by-default in model-gateway weighting before T14 data.

ZDR trap: service-token zdr is a static principal posture (model-gateway and execution-core are always zdr:true toward Quarry). Any future change that reads claim zdr for service callers would silently disable rerank for all chat traffic; conversely trusting only body zdr means a buggy caller can under-declare. Pinned by tests in T09 and recorded in the ledger; an Auth Core change that stamps org posture on service tokens is the robust fix [O-ZDR in O2].

Interactive ZDR resolves to non-ZDR whenever org-core is unreachable (fail to normal retention), so a ZDR org could be reranked via Azure during an outage and the endpoint cannot detect it from the token; platform risk for Auth Core owners (consider never downgrading a recently seen ZDR=true).

Processor and residency basis for sending the QUERY to Azure/Cohere is unverified in the repo (no DPA/ZDR evidence for Cohere-on-Azure; GDPR_SUMMARY prefers Model Plane gating). The fail-closed WEB_RERANK_PROCESSOR_APPROVED flag defaults false; enabling it is a legal decision [O2].

Service-principal pass-through widens the retrieval engine's auth surface; mitigated by a compiled default-deny allowlist, a dedicated scope, a per-route allowed-service list and the auth matrix, but needs a security review before production and must be re-reviewed whenever a route is added to the table.

Production Auth Core refuses allowAnyOrg principals, and every committed principal (including quarry-edge) is allowAnyOrg:true, so none of the cross-plane Quarry paths (ingest, retrieve, rerank) can be authorized in production until fixed org allowlists or an equivalent mechanism exist; this design does not solve it.

Concurrent uncommitted work by other sessions in shared files (plane-service-principals.json, config/README.md, run-control-plane.sh, auth-core token controller/service, Ingestion docker-compose.yml, cost-core cmd/ledger/store/server). Edits must be hunk-level (Edit, not Write), re-read before saving, no stash/checkout; T16 is blocked until the cost-core work lands.

Design 1 (contextual retrieval) will also touch Data Plane migrations, the cost-event verifier (single event type per producer), cost-core visibility and possibly retrieval-engine config; migration timestamps and the verifier change must be coordinated to avoid conflicting edits.

Cost accuracy: the Azure price for Cohere-rerank-v4.0-pro and the billing unit definition are not in the repo; units are estimated and raw quantities are stored so cost can be recomputed; passage windows could change units if documents are long.

Retrieval traces: every non-ZDR Quarry search now also writes a DP retrieval_runs row containing the query text (volume and privacy; purged by the GDPR consumer). The engine also logs raw query text at INFO (existing defect D17); the new endpoint deliberately does not.

Quarry's other Model Plane features (autoprompt default ON, answer, ai-formats, page-title) remain broken after this design unless T17 is done; removing the rerank dependency does not fix them and the compose default keeps autoprompt on.

Quarry cache semantics: degraded results were previously cached for the TTL; the fix depends on carrying rerank status through the provider trait (search_with_report) and every provider implementation keeping its default; a missed call site would reintroduce caching of unreranked results.
HTTP versus gRPC contract drift: SourceRef.url is HTTP-only in this design; if model-gateway later needs it over gRPC the Model Plane protobuf copies must be regenerated together.

Preview/onboarding sentinel org and the global health org: skipping them avoids unattributable cost, but if the owner wants rerank in onboarding previews the shared sentinel needs its own hard rate cap.

Highlight quality depends on SERP snippets being 1-3 sentences; for such documents the passage step often adds nothing (omitted by the not-the-whole-text rule), and the judged set may show it is only valuable for DP chunk text and local-index hits; fallback is mode none with no loss of scores.

owner_decisions.question: O1. Provider capacity: share the existing Azure Foundry Cohere-rerank-v4.0-pro deployment between tenant retrieval and web search, or provision a dedicated deployment (own quota and key) for web rerank?
owner_decisions.options: (a) share with the limiter and reserved retrieval permits; (b) dedicated Azure deployment for web traffic; (c) share now, dedicated before general availability
owner_decisions.recommended: (c): ship on the shared deployment with the provider limiter, and provision a dedicated deployment before GA (also gives an independent kill switch and cost line).

owner_decisions.question: O2. ZDR and legal basis for rerank. Cohere-on-Azure has no ZDR evidence in the repo. What should ZDR/sovereign orgs get, and who confirms the processor basis for sending the query text to Azure/Cohere?
owner_decisions.options: (a) skip with explicit marker (never silent) and keep it that way; (b) pursue a written Microsoft/Cohere no-retention commitment and enable the dark attestation path (RERANK_ZDR_ATTESTATION_*) so ZDR orgs can use it; (c) build a self-hosted text cross-encoder sidecar as profile web-v1-sovereign for ZDR/sovereign orgs (no egress); also decide whether Auth Core should stamp the org's real ZDR on service tokens
owner_decisions.recommended: (a) now, with (b) started in parallel and (c) as the durable answer for ZDR/sovereign orgs; legal must confirm the Art. 28 basis before WEB_RERANK_PROCESSOR_APPROVED is set true. Consistent with the rule that ZDR is respected and only per-connection BYO routes may turn it off for their own runs; rerank never uses a BYO or subscription route.

owner_decisions.question: O3. Which corpus does Quarry's vector leg search?

owner_decisions.recommended: (a). Live corpus shows (b) would surface the org-visible SharePoint document in web results; (c) is more isolation than needed today.

owner_decisions.question: O4. Highlight strategy replacing the LLM sentence.
owner_decisions.options: (a) extractive passage windows scored by the same cross-encoder in the same call; (b) lexical term-coverage sentence only (free, weaker); (c) a separate optional second provider step; (d) none
owner_decisions.recommended: (a), with (b) as the automatic fallback when the 100-document cap trims windows; confirm with the T14 highlight-precision metric.
